title: Ok shifted divisor
statement: How many positive integers $n$ are such that $n + 30$ divides $n^2 + 300$?
hints: The remainder is a constant, so $n + 30$ must be a divisor of it.
solution: Since $n \equiv -30 \pmod{n+30}$, we have $n^2 + 300 \equiv 900 + 300 = 1200 \pmod{n+30}$. So the condition is that $n + 30$ divides $1200$, with $n + 30 > 30$. The number $1200 = 2^4\cdot 3\cdot 5^2$ has $5\cdot 2\cdot 3 = 30$ divisors. They pair up as $d \cdot (1200/d)$. Those at most $30$ are $1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12,15,16,20,24,25,30$, which is $15$ divisors, leaving $15$ above $30$. So there are $15$ values of $n$.

from sympy import divisors
# n + 30 divides n^2 + 300 forces n + 30 to be at most about n^2 + 300, so test n directly up to a generous bound
print(sum(1 for n in range(1, 5000) if (n*n + 300) % (n + 30) == 0))
